_comment: Types round 9 (docs/notes/types_9.md): Grim's Lua state, LState (the remaster's LState::LState), one per task: Lua 3.1's lua_State (stack, C stack, error jump, parser states, C blocks) with the task fields Grim adds (the execution-state chain, break and update flags, the task's function, the task list). Each field from the code that uses it (LState_Construct, lua_updatetasks, luaD_call, luaD_protectedrun, lua_beginblock, lua_error, the parser, lua_pausetasks).

structs.name: CLuaStack
structs.comment: Lua 3.1's C_Lua_Stack: the C function's window on the stack (lapi.c).
fields: first slot of the C function's frame

structs.name: LState
structs.comment: One Lua task (lstate.c LState): g_pLuaState is the running one, g_dwL_Main the first.
fields: the task's chain of execution states (call frames), linked through their +0x0c (lapi.cpp's assert names it L->pExecutionState)
the execution state the task goes on in after luaI_breakhere (luaD_call)
luaI_breakhere yields only while 0; protected and C calls raise it
LState_Construct sets it to 1; nothing reads it
the task ran in this lua_updatetasks round (cleared for every task when a round starts)
lua_pausetasks sets it on every other task, lua_unpausetasks clears it; the updater skips the task
nested luaV_execute calls (warns "Lua nesting level now")
the setjmp buffer lua_error leaves through
the parser's main FuncState (0x168 bytes, on luaY_parser's stack)
the lexer's state (build/overrides.c: [0] the current character, [1] the input)
the C stacks saved by lua_beginblock
serial number (g_dwLState_numThreads), passed to the task hook
